source: សៀវភៅ 'មធ្យោបាយប្រើប្រាស់ឧបករណ៍ព្រោះជាជួរ' (How to Use the Row/Drum Seeder Tool), presented by an agricultural extension teacher for the Agricultural Productivity Enhancement Project in the West Tonle Sap area (APPP) / CAVAC (Cambodia Agricultural Value Chain program), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries -- Battambang provincial department, 2014
text: Recommended pre-germination technique for seed used in the drum seeder, given as a numbered process: (1) prepare a container of clean water; (2) soak the seed, keeping water temperature moderate rather than hot; (3) after roughly 10 hours of soaking, drain the water off and let the sprouting seed rest, covered, for the sprouts to finish emerging; (4) rinse the sprouted seed again in a bucket of clean water to wash off any sour/fermented smell before loading it into the seeder's seed-metering drum; (5) sow within about 24 hours of starting the soak-and-sprout process so the emerging sprout does not overgrow and tangle in the seeder mechanism. The source stresses that a consistent soak-drain-rinse routine gives quality sprouted seed, and that seed should be sown the same day it finishes sprouting rather than held longer.
